report_meta.tool: QueryTrellis — PostgreSQL Query Performance & Optimization Workbench
report_meta.title: Correlated Subquery vs. CTE LEFT JOIN — Sample Report

database_info.server_version: PostgreSQL 18.6 on x86_64-windows, compiled by msvc-19.44.35228, 64-bit

query.sql_text:
SELECT
    c.customer_id,
    c.email,
    c.segment,
    (
        SELECT COUNT(*)
        FROM orders o
        WHERE o.customer_id = c.customer_id
          AND o.status = 'delivered'
    ) AS delivered_orders
FROM customers c
WHERE c.country = 'India'
LIMIT 100;
query.formatted_sql:
SELECT
  c.customer_id,
  c.email,
  c.segment,
  (
    SELECT
      COUNT(*)
    FROM orders AS o
    WHERE
      o.customer_id = c.customer_id AND o.status = 'delivered'
  ) AS delivered_orders
FROM customers AS c
WHERE
  c.country = 'India'
LIMIT 100;

plan_insights.title: Selective Sequential Scan on Large Table
plan_insights.observation: Seq Scan on 'customers' evaluated Filter (((country)::text = 'India'::text)) and discarded 593 of 693 rows (85.6% filtered out).
plan_insights.interpretation: PostgreSQL read the full heap table because no suitable index matched the filter or the predicate was non-sargable.
plan_insights.recommendation: Review the Filter expression and check Index Recommendations for a targeted B-tree or partial index.

plan_insights.title: Row Cardinality Misestimation (20.07x difference)
plan_insights.observation: Planner estimated 2,007 row(s), but execution produced 100 row(s).
plan_insights.interpretation: Large row misestimates can mislead PostgreSQL into picking Nested Loop instead of Hash Join (or under-allocating hash/sort memory).
plan_insights.recommendation: Run `ANALYZE customers` if statistics are stale, or consider `CREATE STATISTICS` for correlated multi-column filters.

plan_insights.title: High Execution Loop Count (100 loops)
plan_insights.interpretation: Repeated inner execution typically occurs beneath a Nested Loop join or correlated SubPlan. Even fast sub-millisecond scans add up over thousands of loops.
plan_insights.recommendation: Ensure an index exists on the inner join/filter key, or rewrite correlated subqueries into CTE/Hash Joins.

antipatterns.affected_fragment: SELECT COUNT(*) FROM orders AS o WHERE o.customer_id = c.customer_id AND o.status = 'delivered'
antipatterns.explanation: Subquery references outer table alias(es) (c) inside a row-level expression or filter.
antipatterns.performance_impact: If PostgreSQL cannot decorrelate the subquery into a Hash/Merge Join, it executes as a SubPlan once per outer row (high loop count).
antipatterns.when_acceptable: Acceptable when outer result sets are tiny (< 100 rows) with a selective inner index, or when PostgreSQL's planner transforms EXISTS into a Semi Join.
antipatterns.suggested_improvement: Rewrite using a pre-aggregated CTE joined via LEFT JOIN, or a LATERAL / window function expression.

index_recommendations.suggested_sql: CREATE INDEX idx_customers_country_cov ON customers(country) INCLUDE (customer_id, email, segment);
index_recommendations.why_it_helps: Includes projected columns (customer_id, email, segment) as non-key leaf payloads, enabling an Index-Only Scan without visiting the main heap table (once visibility map pages are clean).
index_recommendations.existing_index_status: No existing index on 'customers' has 'country' as leading key.
index_recommendations.write_and_storage_overhead: Larger index leaf pages than a plain single-column index; updates to INCLUDE columns also update the index.
index_recommendations.when_not_helpful: If the table receives heavy UPDATE traffic on the INCLUDE columns, or if queries frequently change projected columns.

index_recommendations.why_it_helps: Allows PostgreSQL to jump directly to matching 'customers.country' entries via Index Scan / Bitmap Index Scan instead of scanning the entire table sequentially.
index_recommendations.existing_index_status: No existing index on 'customers' leads with 'country'.
index_recommendations.write_and_storage_overhead: Increases INSERT/DELETE time slightly and updates on 'country'; adds B-tree disk footprint.
index_recommendations.when_not_helpful: Not beneficial if the query returns a large fraction (>20–30%) of table rows, if the table is small, or if predicates wrap the column in non-sargable functions.

index_recommendations.suggested_sql: CREATE INDEX idx_orders_customer_id_status ON orders(customer_id, status);
index_recommendations.why_it_helps: Follows the Equality-Sort-Range (ESR) B-tree ordering rule: equality keys narrow directly to a contiguous slice while trailing range/sort columns avoid extra filtering or Sort steps.
index_recommendations.existing_index_status: No existing index on 'orders' starts with (customer_id, status).
index_recommendations.write_and_storage_overhead: Adds B-tree maintenance cost on INSERT and on UPDATEs modifying any indexed column; wider keys consume slightly more disk/buffer space than single-column indexes.
index_recommendations.when_not_helpful: Ineffective if the leading equality column has very low selectivity (matching >25% of rows) or if queries omit the leading column.

comparison.baseline_sql:
SELECT
    c.customer_id,
    c.email,
    c.segment,
    (
        SELECT COUNT(*)
        FROM orders o
        WHERE o.customer_id = c.customer_id
          AND o.status = 'delivered'
    ) AS delivered_orders
FROM customers c
WHERE c.country = 'India'
LIMIT 100;
comparison.optimized_sql:
WITH delivered_counts AS (
    SELECT
        customer_id,
        COUNT(*) AS delivered_orders
    FROM orders
    WHERE status = 'delivered'
    GROUP BY customer_id
)
SELECT
    c.customer_id,
    c.email,
    c.segment,
    COALESCE(dc.delivered_orders, 0) AS delivered_orders
FROM customers c
LEFT JOIN delivered_counts dc ON dc.customer_id = c.customer_id
WHERE c.country = 'India'
LIMIT 100;
comparison.verdict_summary: Measured execution time improved by 97.4% (253.224 ms -> 6.645 ms, 38.11x faster).

optimization_notes: Sample optimization report generated directly against querytrellis_sample.
methodology_caveats: Cold vs. Warm Cache: Run 1 may read pages from disk/OS cache (Shared Read Blocks), while subsequent runs hit PostgreSQL Shared Buffers.
Database Load & Concurrency: Concurrent queries, autovacuum, or background checkpoints on the host can introduce run-to-run variance.
Client vs. Server Time: Client-observed round-trip duration includes Python driver and IPC/TCP overhead; PostgreSQL Execution Time isolates server plan execution.
Planner Behavior: Parameter changes, stale statistics, or memory settings (work_mem) can alter plan selection across workloads.
Interpretation: Local benchmark results do not represent guaranteed production throughput under concurrency.
